newsitem.title: UK: UK air passenger traffic seen up 15-27 pct by 2002.
newsitem.headline: UK air passenger traffic seen up 15-27 pct by 2002.

text.p: The number of passengers passing through British airports is expected to grow by between 15 and 27 percent by the year 2001/02 compared with 1996/97, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said on Monday in its annual report.
The number of commercial flights is expected to increase by between 13 and 25 percent over the five-year period, it added.
Demand for air travel is seen growing all the time with the rate in the UK expected to be above that for economic growth, a CAA spokesman said.

"Demand for air travel will continue to grow with all the obvious implications that brings for us, whether in safety or economic regulation or in the provision of air traffic services," CAA chairman Sir Malcolm Field said in a statement.
Turnover for the 1996/97 year increased by 13.3 million pounds to 595 million pounds ($998.9 million).
"Buoyant air traffic volumes and tight costs were the key features underlying the year's financial results," the CAA said in a statement. ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
